prompt:
Is one of pipeline's sinks doing most of the work? How uneven is the load?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: no

By scheduled CPU time, the four sinks share the load closely over the 30.6-second trace:

| Sink thread (TID) | Main CPU | CPU time | Share of sink CPU time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| sink-0 (646556) | 5 | 6.840 s | 25.34% |
| sink-1 (646557) | 6 | 6.908 s | 25.59% |
| sink-2 (646558) | 7 | 6.848 s | 25.36% |
| sink-3 (646559) | 8 | 6.400 s | 23.71% |

The busiest sink, `sink-1`, used about 8% more CPU time than `sink-3`; their shares differ by 1.88 percentage points. Each handled roughly a quarter of the sinks’ combined 27.0 CPU seconds.

All four also made about 29,900 `futex` calls. Their paired calls averaged roughly 0.77–0.79 ms each, with 23.1–23.6 seconds of cumulative call time per thread. That is elapsed syscall time, including waiting, rather than CPU time.

This supports an even CPU load across the sinks. The trace does not include per-sink records or bytes processed, so it cannot establish whether they completed equal amounts of application work.
